intro.html: The dragLimit property keeps a widget inside an area while a player drags it. Its simplest form is a rectangle: minX, maxX, minY, and maxY, measured in the coordinates of the widget's parent. Only dragging is limited. A routine can still move the widget anywhere. What is kept inside is the widget's top left corner unless alignX/alignY pick another point of it, which is what the two examples below are about. A side you leave out is not limited at all.

pieceA.css: background: #e4572e; border-radius: 12px; color: white; font-size: 26px; text-align: center; line-height: 80px;

codeA.css: font-size: 18px; font-family: monospace; white-space: pre-wrap; line-height: 1.35; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.28); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px;

noteA.text: The limits are exactly the rectangle drawn here. So the corner of A reaches its bottom right corner and the piece itself hangs out of the frame by its own width and height. Subtract those if you want the whole widget to stay inside, which is what B does.

pieceB.css: background: #3b82f6; border-radius: 12px; color: white; font-size: 26px; text-align: center; line-height: 80px;

dragLimit.maxX: ${PROPERTY x OF frameB} + ${PROPERTY width OF frameB} - ${PROPERTY width}
dragLimit.maxY: ${PROPERTY y OF frameB} + ${PROPERTY height OF frameB} - ${PROPERTY height}

codeB.css: font-size: 18px; font-family: monospace; white-space: pre-wrap; line-height: 1.35; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.28); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px;

noteB.text: A side can be an expression instead of a number, and a property is read the way a routine reads one. These read the frame and take off B's own size, so B stays completely inside. Use the button to resize the frame and B stays inside the new boundaries. A widget left outside its rectangle is free until it is back inside, so nothing can get stuck.

hintB.html: The limit follows it, without a routine touching dragLimit.
